title: Understanding Mental Health and Wellbeing
summary: Explore what mental health means, what shapes wellbeing, and the ways people can care for themselves and support others.
goals: Explain mental health in plain language and recognize that it is more than the absence of illness.
Describe how feelings, thoughts, relationships, body, circumstances and community influence wellbeing.
Differentiate common emotional experiences, psychological distress and possible mental health conditions without self-diagnosing.
Recognize barriers, protective influences, stigma and situations where professional support is useful.
Identify one realistic action to care for mental wellbeing while recognizing problems that require external support.

title: Recognizing Emotions and Responding to Them
summary: Learn about emotional experiences, practical responses, safe communication, and when additional support may be useful.
goals: Identify common emotions and explain how emotions, thoughts, physical sensations and actions interact.
Recognize that emotions have useful information but do not always represent facts or instructions.
Practise naming feelings and choosing safe responses to them.
Distinguish emotional expression from harmful behavior, suppression and avoidance.
Apply simple grounding, self-kindness and communication skills without treating them as a replacement for healthcare.
Recognize when emotional difficulties warrant routine or urgent professional assistance.

title: Understanding Stress and Healthy Coping Strategies
summary: Explore stress, practical pressures, flexible coping, and when additional support matters.
goals: Explain how a stress response differs from a stressor, and why stress does not always signal illness.
Identify emotional, physical, cognitive, behavioral, and social changes that may accompany stress.
Distinguish manageable short-term stress from prolonged distress that deserves extra support.
Apply several flexible coping skills without blaming oneself for difficult circumstances.
Recognize warning signs indicating the need for professional or urgent medical support.

title: Understanding Anxiety and Anxiety Disorders
summary: Understand everyday anxiety, anxiety disorders, supportive responses, and professional care.
goals: Explain anxiety and why it can be protective in some situations.
Recognize emotional, thinking, physical and behavioral signs of anxiety without self-diagnosing.
Describe major anxiety disorders and distinguish a panic attack from panic disorder.
Practice optional coping skills while understanding their limitations.
Recognize when professional or emergency assessment is appropriate.
Support someone experiencing anxiety with respect and without judgment.

title: Understanding Depression and Depressive Disorders
summary: Learn about depression, compassionate support, treatment, and small steps that respect individual circumstances.
goals: Explain the difference between ordinary sadness, grief and a depressive disorder.
Recognize emotional, cognitive, physical, behavioral and safety-related warning signs.
Understand major depressive disorder and other relevant depressive presentations without self-diagnosing.
Identify evidence-based professional treatments and the supportive role of self-care.
Practice low-pressure strategies that support daily functioning and help-seeking.
Respond compassionately and safely when someone may be depressed or at risk of suicide.

title: Understanding Trauma and Post-Traumatic Stress
summary: Explore trauma responses, safety, voluntary coping, and pathways to appropriate professional support.
goals: Explain trauma, common stress reactions, acute stress disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in plain language.
Recognize the core symptom patterns of PTSD without assuming that symptoms confirm a diagnosis.
Identify practical, low-intensity coping options and the limits of self-help.
Describe evidence-based treatment and understand when and how to seek professional or emergency support.
Respond to a person affected by trauma respectfully, without pressuring them to disclose their experiences.

title: Understanding Grief, Loss, and Emotional Adjustment
summary: Understand different losses, changing grief experiences, practical support, and when assessment may help.
goals: Describe grief, bereavement, mourning, and emotional adjustment in plain language.
Recognize emotional, physical, cognitive, social, and practical responses to loss.
Understand why grieving does not follow a fixed set of stages or a universal timetable.
Identify compassionate coping methods, helpful support, and ways to assist another person.
Distinguish ordinary grief from situations needing assessment, including prolonged grief disorder.
